- When sentiment is negative and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true values after a recent price spike, apply a downward bias of 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is flat or slightly declining, increase the mean by 1–3% to capture momentum.  
- If true price deviates from forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust future forecasts toward the mean of the last 7-day window.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently negative, apply a 1–2% downward bias to the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.  
- If forecast shows a sharp drop followed by a rebound, expect a lagged rebound — delay the upward correction by 1–2 days.
